text: So, just to kick things off, could you walk me through your background, and what's brought you over to Australia?
rephrase: Tell me about yourself. What is your experience, and why did you come to Australia?
gist: Tell me about your background and why you came to Australia.
distractors: Tell me about your plans for the next five years in Australia.
Explain why you left your last job.

text: Tell us a bit about yourself. What's your story?
rephrase: Tell me about yourself.
gist: Tell me about yourself.
distractors: Tell me a story about your last project.
What do you do in your free time?

phrases.meaning: tell me about your life and career

text: So what's got you interested in this role, out of all the ones going around at the moment?
rephrase: Why are you interested in this job, when there are many other jobs available?
gist: Why do you want this particular job?
distractors: Which other jobs have you applied for?
What do you know about our company?

text: What do you know about us as a company, if anything?
rephrase: What do you know about our company?
gist: What do you know about our company?
distractors: Have you used our product before?
Do you know anyone who works here?

phrases.meaning: it's okay if you know nothing

text: How'd you go settling in? Have you been here long?
rephrase: How is life in Australia so far? How long have you been here?
gist: How long have you been in Australia, and how is it going?
distractors: Where do you plan to live?
Do you have family here?

phrases.meaning: getting used to a new place

text: Where do you see yourself in, say, three to five years' time?
rephrase: What are your career goals for the next three to five years?
gist: What are your career goals for the next few years?
distractors: How long did you stay in your last three jobs?
When will you be ready to start?

text: Give us the quick rundown of your current role. What does a typical day look like?
rephrase: Briefly describe your current job. What do you do on a normal day?
gist: Describe your current job and a normal workday.
distractors: How many hours do you work each day?
What would your ideal job look like?

phrases.meaning: give me (Australians often say us for me)

text: What would your old manager say is your biggest strength?
rephrase: What would your previous boss say you are best at?
gist: What would your last manager say you do best?
distractors: Why did you leave your old manager?
What is your manager's biggest strength?

text: And what's something you're still working on, professionally speaking?
rephrase: What is a weakness you are trying to improve at work?
gist: What work skill are you still trying to improve?
distractors: What project are you working on right now?
What do you do outside work?

text: What made you want to get into this line of work in the first place?
rephrase: Why did you choose this career?
gist: Why did you choose this career?
distractors: When did you first start working?
Would you like to change careers?

text: Is there anything on your resume you reckon we should dig into a bit more?
rephrase: Is there something on your CV you want to talk about in more detail?
gist: What part of your CV should we discuss in more detail?
distractors: Can you send us your resume again?
Is there a mistake on your resume?

text: How do you like to unwind outside of work?
rephrase: What do you do to relax after work?
gist: What do you do to relax outside work?
distractors: Do you often work late?
How do you get to work?

text: What sort of team do you work best in? Big, small, a bit of both?
rephrase: What kind of team do you prefer?
gist: What size and type of team suits you best?
distractors: How many people did you manage?
Who was the best person in your team?

text: Have you had any experience working with Aussie companies before, or would this be your first?
rephrase: Have you worked for an Australian company before?
gist: Have you worked for an Australian company before?
distractors: Is this your first job?
Have you visited Australia before?

text: Before we get stuck into it, how's your day been so far?
rephrase: Before we start, how is your day going?
gist: Small talk: how is your day going?
distractors: Are you ready to start work today?
Did you find our office easily?

text: Can you tell me about a time you tracked down a really tricky bug? And how did you go about raising it with the devs?
rephrase: Tell me about a difficult bug you found. How did you investigate it, and how did you tell the developers?
gist: Describe a hard bug you found, and how you reported it to developers.
distractors: Describe a bug that a developer found in your tests.
Explain how you would train new developers.

text: Righto, last one from me. If a developer pushes back and reckons your bug isn't really a bug, how do you handle that?
rephrase: Last question. If a developer says your bug is not a real bug, what do you do?
gist: What do you do when a developer says your bug is not a real bug?
distractors: What do you do when you cannot reproduce a bug?
What was the last bug you reported?

text: The team's spread across a few time zones, so there isn't a heap of overlap. How would you keep everyone on the same page?
rephrase: The team works in different time zones. How would you keep communication clear?
gist: How would you keep a team in different time zones informed?
distractors: Are you happy to work night shifts?
How many people were in your last team?

text: Tell me about a time you had to work to a really tight deadline. How'd you go?
rephrase: Describe a time you had very little time to finish work. How did it go?
gist: Tell me about working to a very short deadline and the result.
distractors: How do you plan your work for the week?
Have you ever missed a deadline on purpose?

text: Can you think of a time you stuffed something up at work? What happened, and what did you learn?
rephrase: Tell me about a mistake you made at work and what you learned.
gist: Describe a mistake you made at work and what you learned.
distractors: Tell me about a mistake your colleague made.
How do you check your work for mistakes?

phrases.phrase: can you think of a time

text: Walk me through a time you had to deal with a difficult stakeholder.
rephrase: Tell me step by step about a time you worked with a difficult person, like a manager or client.
gist: Describe working with a difficult manager or client.
distractors: Who are the stakeholders in your current project?
How do you deal with stress?

phrases.meaning: a person who cares about the result: client, manager, product owner

text: Have you ever had to juggle a few competing priorities? How did you decide what to tackle first?
rephrase: Have you had many important tasks at once? How did you choose what to do first?
gist: How do you choose what to do first when several tasks are urgent?
distractors: Do you like to work on many projects at once?
Which task do you enjoy the most?

text: Tell me about a time you went above and beyond for a customer or your team.
rephrase: Tell me about a time you did more than you had to.
gist: Describe a time you did more than was expected.
distractors: How many hours a week do you usually work?
Tell me about your best customer.

text: Give me an example of when you disagreed with your manager. How did you handle it?
rephrase: Tell me about a disagreement with your manager. What did you do?
gist: Describe a disagreement with your manager and how you handled it.
distractors: Why did you change managers?
What do you like about your manager?

text: How do you go about getting up to speed on something you know nothing about?
rephrase: How do you learn something completely new?
gist: How do you learn a new topic quickly?
distractors: How do you explain something new to others?
What new technology do you want to learn?

text: Tell me about a time things didn't go to plan on a project. What did you do?
rephrase: Tell me about a project problem and how you reacted.
gist: Describe a project that went wrong and what you did.
distractors: How do you plan a new project?
Tell me about your favourite project.

text: Have you ever had to give a colleague some tough feedback? How'd you approach that?
rephrase: Did you ever have to tell a coworker something negative about their work? How did you do it?
gist: How did you give difficult feedback to a colleague?
distractors: How do you react to negative feedback?
How often do you have team meetings?

text: What's an achievement you're really proud of, and why does it stand out for you?
rephrase: What is your proudest achievement, and why is it special for you?
gist: What achievement are you most proud of, and why?
distractors: What award did your company win?
Why do you want to stand out in the team?

phrases.meaning: be special, different from the rest

text: Say you've got a heap on your plate and your manager drops another urgent task on you. What do you do?
rephrase: You are already very busy and your manager gives you another urgent task. What do you do?
gist: What do you do when you are very busy and get another urgent task?
distractors: How do you ask your manager for more work?
What do you do when there's no work?

text: Tell me about a time you had to explain something technical to someone who wasn't across the details.
rephrase: Tell me about explaining a technical topic to a non-technical person.
gist: Describe explaining something technical to a non-technical person.
distractors: Tell me about a technical course you took.
How do you write technical documentation?

text: What are you looking for, salary wise? And just to be clear, is that base, or are we talking package, including super?
rephrase: What salary do you expect? Is that without superannuation, or including it?
gist: What salary do you expect, and does it include super?
distractors: How much did you earn in your last job?
Do you need visa sponsorship?

phrases.meaning: salary plus super and other benefits

text: And what's your availability like? What sort of notice period are we looking at?
rephrase: When can you start? Do you need to give notice to your current employer?
gist: When can you start, and what is your notice period?
distractors: Which days of the week are you free for an interview?
How long did you stay in your last job?

phrases.meaning: when you are free to start
time you must work after you resign

phrases.phrase: what sort of... are we looking at

text: Are you after full-time, part-time, or are you open to contract work?
rephrase: Do you want full-time, part-time, or contract work?
gist: What type of employment do you want?
distractors: How many hours did you work last week?
Do you have a contract with your current employer?

text: Do you have full working rights in Australia?
rephrase: Are you allowed to work in Australia without limits?
gist: Are you legally allowed to work in Australia?
distractors: Do you have a driver's licence?
Have you worked in Australia before?

text: How would you feel about coming into the office a couple of days a week?
rephrase: Are you okay working in the office two days a week?
gist: Are you okay with working in the office two days a week?
distractors: How long does it take you to get to the office?
Would you like to work from home full-time?

text: Are you okay with the occasional bit of after-hours work around releases?
rephrase: Can you sometimes work in the evening when there is a release?
gist: Can you sometimes work after hours during releases?
distractors: How often do you release software?
Do you want overtime pay?

text: We'd be looking at a probation period of six months. Is that alright with you?
rephrase: The first six months are a trial period. Is that okay?
gist: Do you accept a six-month probation period?
distractors: Can you start in six months?
Did you have probation in your last job?

phrases.meaning: trial period at the start of a job

text: Have you got any holidays booked in the next few months that we should know about?
rephrase: Do you have any planned holidays soon?
gist: Do you have any planned holidays soon?
distractors: How many holidays do you want per year?
Where did you go on your last holiday?

text: Just so you know, the budget for this role sits around ninety to a hundred K plus super. Does that work for you?
rephrase: The salary is about 90 to 100 thousand dollars plus super. Is that okay?
gist: Is a salary of 90 to 100 thousand plus super okay for you?
distractors: How much super did you get in your last job?
Can you work for 90 to 100 days?

text: Would you need any sponsorship, now or down the track?
rephrase: Will you need visa sponsorship now or in the future?
gist: Will you need visa sponsorship now or later?
distractors: Do you need help moving to a new city?
Who will sponsor this project?

text: Are you currently interviewing anywhere else?
rephrase: Do you have interviews with other companies now?
gist: Are you interviewing with other companies?
distractors: Have you interviewed people before?
Where else have you worked?

text: If we made you an offer, how soon could you kick off?
rephrase: If we offer you the job, when can you start?
gist: How soon can you start if you get an offer?
distractors: What offer would you accept?
How soon can you finish this interview?

text: Are you happy for us to reach out to a couple of your referees?
rephrase: Can we contact some of your references?
gist: Can we contact your references?
distractors: Can you send us a few work examples?
Can you refer a friend for this job?

phrases.meaning: people who give you a reference

text: Whereabouts are you based? Is the commute going to be a problem?
rephrase: Where do you live? Will travelling to the office be difficult?
gist: Where do you live, and is travel to the office a problem?
distractors: Where were you born?
Do you have a car?

phrases.meaning: the trip to work and back

text: Just to manage expectations, the next step would be a technical chat with the team. That suit you?
rephrase: The next stage is a technical interview with the team. Is that okay?
gist: Are you okay with a technical interview as the next step?
distractors: Can you manage the team's expectations?
Would you like to chat with the team at lunch?

phrases.meaning: an informal talk, often an interview

text: Have you had much exposure to mocking in your test setup? And how do you make sure your automated tests are actually reliable, and not flaky?
rephrase: Do you use mocks in your tests? And how do you make your automated tests stable?
gist: Have you used mocks, and how do you keep automated tests stable?
distractors: How many automated tests have you written?
Which test framework do you like the most?

text: Fair enough. Have you had a crack at testing anything A.I. driven, like L.L.M. features, or agents? No worries if not.
rephrase: Have you tested any AI features, for example LLMs or AI agents? It's okay if you haven't.
gist: Have you tested AI features like LLMs or agents?
distractors: Do you use AI tools to write your tests?
What do you think about AI replacing testers?

text: How would you go about testing a login screen if we gave you, say, twenty minutes?
rephrase: How would you test a login screen in twenty minutes?
gist: How would you test a login screen in a short time?
distractors: How long does it take you to log in?
Have you ever designed a login screen?

text: Where do you sit on the whole manual versus automation debate?
rephrase: What is your opinion about manual testing compared to automation?
gist: What do you think about manual versus automated testing?
distractors: How many manual testers were in your last team?
Which automation tool is the most popular?

text: How do you decide what's worth automating and what's not?
rephrase: How do you choose which tests to automate?
gist: How do you choose which tests to automate?
distractors: How long does it take to automate a test?
Which tests have you deleted?

text: Talk me through how you'd write up a bug so a dev can pick it up straight away.
rephrase: How do you write a bug report so a developer understands it immediately?
gist: How do you write a clear bug report?
distractors: How do you pick which bugs to fix first?
How fast do developers fix your bugs?

text: What's your take on testing in production? Ever done it?
rephrase: What do you think about testing on the live system? Have you done it?
gist: What do you think about testing in production?
distractors: Have you ever caused a production incident?
How often do you release to production?

phrases.meaning: on the live system real users use

text: How do you get your head around a new codebase or product quickly?
rephrase: How do you understand a new product or code quickly?
gist: How do you learn a new product or codebase quickly?
distractors: How do you write code faster?
Which products do you use every day?

text: Have you worked much with APIs? What tools do you reach for?
rephrase: Do you have experience testing APIs? Which tools do you use?
gist: What is your API testing experience, and which tools do you use?
distractors: Have you designed an API yourself?
Which tools does your team need?

text: How do you fit into a CI pipeline? Like, where do your tests actually run?
rephrase: How do your tests work in CI? Where are they executed?
gist: Where and how do your automated tests run in CI?
distractors: How do you build the pipeline for developers?
How long have you used CI?

text: If you only had half a day for regression before a release, what would you focus on?
rephrase: You have four hours for regression testing before release. What do you test?
gist: What would you test with very little regression time?
distractors: How long does your regression usually take?
Would you delay the release by half a day?

text: How do you deal with a test that passes on your machine but keeps falling over in the pipeline?
rephrase: A test passes locally but fails in CI. What do you do?
gist: What do you do when a test passes locally but fails in CI?
distractors: How do you set up your local machine?
How do you deal with a broken laptop?

text: Have you had a go at performance or load testing at all?
rephrase: Have you tried performance or load testing?
gist: Do you have performance or load testing experience?
distractors: How do you improve your own performance at work?
How much load can you handle at work?

text: How do you work out the acceptance criteria when the ticket's a bit thin?
rephrase: How do you find the requirements when a task has little detail?
gist: How do you clarify requirements when a ticket has few details?
distractors: How do you write a ticket for developers?
How do you close tickets faster?

phrases.meaning: conditions that show a task is done

text: What does a good test strategy look like to you, in a nutshell?
rephrase: Briefly, what is a good test strategy?
gist: Briefly describe a good test strategy.
distractors: Who writes the test strategy in your team?
What does your test environment look like?
